title: improving the coding agent
description:
## Improving the Coding Agent — CompletionTools

A recent new project has emerged: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode

Well known coding agents available for comparison:
- Claude Code: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/overview
- Cursor: https://cursor.com/docs
- Codex: https://github.com/openai/codex
- Roo Code, Gemini CLI, Pi, OpenHands (open-source; studied via compaction teardown)

---

### Competitor Research (completed)

A full competitor analysis has been written to `docs/COMPETITOR_IMPROVEMENTS.md`. Key findings:

**All competitors avoid receipt-shaped JSON in tool argument history.** They replace pruned content with plain human-readable strings (`[Old tool result content cleared]`, `[Tool result cleared]`) — never with structured JSON objects the model could mimic.

**OpenCode's edit tool uses exact-string replacement (no line numbers).** Line-number drift is architecturally impossible. They also embed batching guidance directly in every tool description.

**Claude Code has 5 compaction mechanisms** including a zero-latency microcompact that runs every turn (no LLM call) clearing old tool results. Also re-injects recently-read files post-compaction.

**Cursor reports 46.9% token reduction** from dynamic context discovery — minimal context upfront, lazy tool-fetch. KV cache stays warm on the stable prefix indefinitely.

**KV cache economics:** A warm cache read costs ~1/10th of a cold token. One compaction event on 125k tokens ≈ $0.40 in cache-miss cost = 21 follow-up warm turns. Our aggressive `keepLastTurns=5` is busting the cache too early.

---

### The Four Core Problems (confirmed by research)

| # | Problem | Root Cause (our stack) | Competitor Solution |
|---|---------|------------------------|---------------------|
| 1 | **High token cost** | 3-phase tool flow, aggressive summarisation at turn 5, no inline prune | Microcompact (no LLM), dynamic lazy context, keep 15–20 turns before summarising |
| 2 | **Many small tools vs one wide one** | Batching instruction only in system prompt, not in tool descriptions | OpenCode embeds "prefer batch reads" in every tool's `description` field |
| 3 | **Diff/patch hallucinations** | `writeDiffToFile` requires exact line numbers; stale history causes drift | OpenCode `edit`: exact string replace (no line numbers); Claude Code re-injects fresh files post-compaction |
| 4 | **`writeFile` gets `{__system_omitted:true}` as content** | `sanitizeMessagesForLLM` puts receipt JSON inside write tool *arguments*; model mimics it | All competitors: replace with plain string, never JSON; guard at tool execution layer |

---

### Plan (Prioritised)

**P0 — Fix receipt-in-arguments (Problem 4)**
- Replace receipt JSON with human-readable strings in write-tool argument sanitisation
- Add post-condition guard in `writeFile` that rejects `__system_omitted`-shaped content

**P1 — Exact-string-replace edit tool (Problem 3)**
- Implement `writeExactReplace` — `{path, search, replace}`, no line numbers
- Add line-number prefixes to `readFileRange`/`readPaths` output

**P2 — Batching in tool descriptions (Problem 2)**
- Update every tool description with batching preference + cross-tool guidance
- Add composite tool (e.g., `grepAndRead`) for single-round-trip results

**P3 — No-LLM inline prune pass (Problem 1)**
- Implement microcompact: before every `sendCompletion`, clear old tool results beyond protected window using plain strings (no LLM, no latency)
- Increase `keepLastTurns` from 5 to 15–20

**P4 — Three-phase → single-phase (Problem 1)**
- Eliminate starter/finalizer phases; move to pure native-tool loop

**P5 — Cache observability (Problem 1)**
- Surface `cachedReadInputTokens` ratio in dashboards; alert on cache-hit ratio drops

**P6 — Structured compaction prompt (anti-drift)**
- Adopt 9-section structured prompt pattern for LLM-assisted summarisation

Full analysis: `docs/COMPETITOR_IMPROVEMENTS.md`

features.title: P0 — Fix receipt-in-write-arguments: human-readable replacement + execution guard
features.description:
## Problem

`sanitizeMessagesForLLM` in `src/completion/completionMessageSanitizer.ts` calls `makeTruncationReceipt()` to replace large `content`/`diff` fields in old **write-tool call arguments** with a structured JSON object:

```json
{ "__system_omitted": true, "originalChars": 52400 }
```

The model then sees this object in prior `writeFile` / `writeDiffToFile` / `writeStrictPatch` argument history and **mimics it** on the next write — producing `writeFile` calls whose `content` is literally `{"__system_omitted":true,"originalChars":N}` rather than real file content.

No competitor studied puts a JSON receipt object inside tool *call arguments*. They only prune tool *results/outputs*. OpenCode uses `[Old tool result content cleared]`, Claude Code uses `[Tool result cleared]` — plain strings the model cannot plausibly mistake for valid file content.

---

## Changes Required

### 1. `src/completion/completionMessageSanitizer.ts` — replace receipt JSON with plain string for write-tool arguments

In `sanitizeToolArguments`, when the write-tool argument key being sanitised is `content`, `diff`, `patch`, or `data` **and** the tool is a write tool (`writeFile`, `writeDiffToFile`, `writeStrictPatch`, `writeFuzzyPatch`, `writeStructuredDiffToFile`), replace with:

```ts
"[Content omitted — file was written to disk. Re-read the file if needed.]"
```

instead of calling `makeTruncationReceiptString(chars)`.

The sanitizer already has the tool name available via the message context when iterating. If the tool name is not yet threaded through, thread it: the call site in `sanitizeMessagesForLLM` processes `CompletionToolMessage` objects which have `message.toolCall.name`.

The set of write-tool names to guard against should be a named constant (e.g. `WRITE_TOOL_NAMES`) importable by both the sanitizer and the guard (below).

### 2. `src/file/FileTools.ts` — execution-time guard in `writeFile`

Before executing the write, check if the `content` argument is a string that JSON-parses into a `__system_omitted`-shaped receipt:

```ts
function isOmissionReceipt(content: string): boolean {
  if (!content.startsWith('{')) return false
  try {
    const parsed = JSON.parse(content)
    return parsed != null && typeof parsed === 'object' && '__system_omitted' in parsed
  } catch {
    return false
  }
}
```

If detected, **throw** (or return a structured error string) before touching the filesystem:

```
"Invalid content: omission receipt detected — the model passed a history placeholder as file content. Re-read the target file and provide the actual content."
```

This guard should also be applied to `writeDiffToFile` / `writeStrictPatch` / `writeFuzzyPatch` for their `diff` parameter (same check).

### 3. Tests — `src/completion/completionMessageSanitizer.test.ts` and `src/file/FileTools.test.ts`

All tests must follow `docs/TESTING.md`: one test per code path, atomic, offline, using temp dirs, mocking all external I/O.

#### `src/completion/completionMessageSanitizer.test.ts`

Each test is a single `it` with one focused assertion:

- **Write-tool arg omission emits plain string**: for a `writeFile` tool message with a `content` arg that exceeds `maxToolArgChars`, confirm the sanitised argument value is exactly `"[Content omitted — file was written to disk. Re-read the file if needed.]"` — not a JSON object.
- **All WRITE_TOOL_NAMES trigger plain-string replacement**: repeat the above for each tool in `WRITE_TOOL_NAMES` (`writeDiffToFile`→`diff`, `writeStrictPatch`→`diff`, `writeFuzzyPatch`→`diff`, `writeStructuredDiffToFile`→`diff`). One test per tool name.
- **Non-write tool large args still emit JSON receipt**: for a non-write tool (e.g. `readPaths`) with oversized args, confirm the receipt object still contains `__system_omitted: true` (existing behaviour unchanged).
- **Write-tool arg below threshold is untouched**: for a `writeFile` message whose `content` arg is within `maxToolArgChars`, confirm the argument is passed through verbatim (no replacement).
- **Write-tool arg within protected tail is untouched**: for a `writeFile` message that is inside `keepLastMessages`, confirm its `content` arg is not replaced even if it exceeds the char limit.

#### `src/file/FileTools.test.ts`

Each test is a single `it`:

- **`writeFile` rejects receipt-shaped content**: calling `tools.writeFile` with `'{"__system_omitted":true,"originalChars":500}'` as content throws (or returns an error string containing `"omission receipt"`); the file is not created on disk.
- **`writeFile` accepts normal content after guard check**: calling `tools.writeFile` with ordinary string content still succeeds (regression guard).
- **`writeDiffToFile` rejects receipt-shaped diff**: calling `tools.writeDiffToFile` with a receipt-shaped `diff` string throws/errors before touching the file.
- **`writeStrictPatch` rejects receipt-shaped diff**: same guard for `writeStrictPatch`.
- **`writeFuzzyPatch` rejects receipt-shaped diff**: same guard for `writeFuzzyPatch`.

---

## Acceptance Criteria

- `writeFile` called with `'{"__system_omitted":true,"originalChars":500}'` as content throws before writing.
- In sanitised history, a `writeFile` message whose `content` arg exceeded `maxToolArgChars` shows the plain string `[Content omitted — file was written to disk. Re-read the file if needed.]` — never a JSON receipt object.
- Non-write tool large args continue to use the existing receipt JSON (no regression).
- All existing sanitizer + FileTools tests continue to pass.

---

## Files

- `src/completion/completionMessageSanitizer.ts`
- `src/completion/completionMessageSanitizer.test.ts`
- `src/file/FileTools.ts`
- `src/file/FileTools.test.ts`

features.title: P1.3 — Add `writeExactReplace` tool: exact-string-replace, no line numbers
features.description:
## Problem

`writeDiffToFile` requires a git-style unified diff with exact hunk headers (`@@ -L,N +L,N @@`). Any line-number drift from history summarisation or stale context causes the patch to fail or corrupt silently.

OpenCode's `edit` tool avoids this entirely: the model provides an exact `search` string (the text to find) and a `replace` string (the replacement). No line numbers. No hunk headers. The server finds the exact match in the current file, applies it, and rejects the call if the search string is not found or is ambiguous.

---

## New Tool: `writeExactReplace`

### Signature

```ts
writeExactReplace(
  path: string,
  search: string,
  replace: string,
  dryRun?: boolean,
): Promise<string>
```

**Parameters:**
- `path` — project-relative path to the file to edit.
- `search` — exact substring to find in the current file. Must match verbatim (no regex, no trimming). If the string appears zero times → error. If it appears more than once → error (ambiguous).
- `replace` — the string to substitute in place of `search`. May be empty (deletion).
- `dryRun` — if `true`, validate and compute the diff but do not write to disk.

**Returns:** A unified diff string (same as `writeFile` and `writeDiffToFile`) showing what changed.

**Errors (returned as thrown Error or error string, same pattern as the other write tools):**
- `"writeExactReplace: search string not found in file."` — zero matches.
- `"writeExactReplace: search string is ambiguous (N occurrences). Make the search string more specific."` — more than one match.

---

## Implementation in `src/file/FileTools.ts`

Add a new internal async function `writeExactReplace`:

```ts
async function writeExactReplace(
  root: string,
  path: string,
  search: string,
  replace: string,
  dryRun: boolean = false,
): Promise<string> {
  const abs = nodepath.resolve(root, path)
  if (!isWithinRoot(root, abs))
    throw new Error(`Security violation: Attempt to write outside of project root: ${path}`)

  const oldContent = await fsp.readFile(abs, 'utf8')

  // Count occurrences
  const occurrences = countOccurrences(oldContent, search)
  if (occurrences === 0)
    throw new Error('writeExactReplace: search string not found in file.')
  if (occurrences > 1)
    throw new Error(
      `writeExactReplace: search string is ambiguous (${occurrences} occurrences). Make the search string more specific.`,
    )

  const newContent = oldContent.replace(search, replace)

  if (!dryRun && oldContent !== newContent) {
    await fsp.writeFile(abs, newContent, 'utf8')
  }

  return createPatch(path, oldContent, newContent)
}

function countOccurrences(haystack: string, needle: string): number {
  if (!needle) return 0
  let count = 0
  let pos = 0
  while ((pos = haystack.indexOf(needle, pos)) !== -1) {
    count++
    pos += needle.length
  }
  return count
}
```

Expose it in `createFileTools`:
```ts
writeExactReplace: (path: string, search: string, replace: string, dryRun?: boolean) =>
  writeExactReplace(ROOT, path, search, replace, !!dryRun),
```

---

## Interface in `src/file/fileTypes.ts`

Add to `FileTools`:

```ts
/**
 * Edit a file by replacing an exact string match. No line numbers required.
 *
 * The `search` string must appear **exactly once** in the current file content.
 * - If it appears zero times → error: 'search string not found'.
 * - If it appears more than once → error: 'search string is ambiguous'.
 *
 * This is the preferred edit tool for targeted changes because it is immune
 * to line-number drift caused by prior edits or summarised history.
 *
 * Prefer this over `writeDiffToFile` whenever you are replacing a specific
 * known block of code rather than a line-range hunk.
 *
 * @param path Project-relative path.
 * @param search Exact substring to find (verbatim, no regex).
 * @param replace Replacement string (may be empty to delete the matched text).
 * @param dryRun If true, validate and compute the diff but do not write.
 * @example
 * const diff = await files.writeExactReplace(
 *   'src/utils.ts',
 *   'export const OLD_CONST = 1',
 *   'export const NEW_CONST = 2',
 * )
 */
writeExactReplace(
  path: string,
  search: string,
  replace: string,
  dryRun?: boolean,
): Promise<string>
```

---

## Tests in `src/file/FileTools.test.ts`

All tests must follow `docs/TESTING.md`: one test per code path, atomic, offline, using temp dirs, mocking all external I/O.

Each of the following is a separate `it` block:

- **Happy path — single occurrence replaced**: create a file with one match, call `writeExactReplace`, verify the returned diff is non-empty and shows the change; verify the file on disk has the new content.
- **Zero occurrences → search-not-found error**: call `writeExactReplace` with a search string that doesn't exist in the file; expect the error message to contain `"search string not found"`.
- **Multiple occurrences → ambiguous error**: create a file with two identical blocks; call `writeExactReplace`; expect the error to contain `"is ambiguous"` and the occurrence count.
- **`dryRun=true` — no file written, diff returned**: call with `dryRun: true`; the diff is returned but the file on disk is unchanged.
- **Empty replace string deletes matched text**: replace a substring with `""` and verify the text is removed from the file.
- **Multiline search+replace**: `search` spans multiple lines; verify correct substitution and that surrounding content is intact.
- **Security — path outside root throws**: pass a path that traverses outside the project root; expect a security-violation error before any filesystem access.
- **Non-existent file throws**: call on a path that doesn't exist; expect a file-not-found error.

---

## Files

- `src/file/FileTools.ts`
- `src/file/fileTypes.ts`
- `src/file/FileTools.test.ts`

features.title: P1.4 — Add optional line-number prefixes to `readPaths` and `readFileRange` output
features.description:
## Problem

When the model reads a file and then tries to use `writeDiffToFile`, it must produce exact line numbers. But nothing in the `readPaths` or `readFileRange` output tells the model *which* line number each line is. The model has to count manually — and gets it wrong after any prior edit shifts the file.

Adding optional 1-based line-number prefixes to file content output gives the model precise anchors and eliminates guessing.

---

## Changes

### 1. `src/file/fileTypes.ts` — extend `FileTools` signatures

Add an optional `lineNumbers` parameter to both tools:

```ts
/**
 * Read multiple files and return their contents keyed by path.
 *
 * @param paths Array of project-relative paths to read.
 * @param lineNumbers If true, each line of every file is prefixed with its
 *   1-based line number in the format `"  42 | <content>"`.
 *   This makes it safe to use the returned content as a reference when
 *   constructing `writeDiffToFile` or `writeExactReplace` arguments —
 *   the model can read the line number directly rather than counting.
 *   The prefix is NOT part of the file's actual content and must not be
 *   included in any write-tool argument.
 * @example
 * // Without line numbers (default):
 * // { "src/a.ts": "const x = 1\nconst y = 2\n" }
 *
 * // With line numbers:
 * // { "src/a.ts": "   1 | const x = 1\n   2 | const y = 2\n" }
 */
readPaths(paths: string[], lineNumbers?: boolean): Promise<Record<string, string>>

/**
 * Read a specific line range from a file.
 *
 * Prefer `readPaths` for full files. Use `readFileRanges` when you need
 * sections from multiple files in a single round-trip.
 *
 * @param path Project-relative path.
 * @param startLine 1-based start line (inclusive).
 * @param endLine 1-based end line (inclusive).
 * @param lineNumbers If true, each returned line is prefixed with its actual
 *   1-based line number in the file (not relative to startLine), in the
 *   format `"  42 | <content>"`. Useful when you need exact anchor lines
 *   for subsequent edits. The prefix must NOT be included in any write-tool
 *   argument content.
 */
readFileRange(path: string, startLine: number, endLine: number, lineNumbers?: boolean): Promise<string>
```

### 2. `src/file/FileTools.ts` — implement the formatting

Add a pure helper:

```ts
/**
 * Prefix each line with its 1-based absolute line number.
 * Format: right-aligned in a 4-char field, e.g. "   1 | ..."
 */
function prefixLineNumbers(content: string, startLineOffset: number = 1): string {
  const lines = content.split('\n')
  // Trailing newline produces an empty last element — remove it before numbering
  const hasTrailingNewline = lines[lines.length - 1] === ''
  const toNumber = hasTrailingNewline ? lines.slice(0, -1) : lines
  const maxWidth = String(startLineOffset + toNumber.length - 1).length
  const numbered = toNumber.map(
    (line, i) => `${String(startLineOffset + i).padStart(Math.max(maxWidth, 4), ' ')} | ${line}`,
  )
  return hasTrailingNewline ? numbered.join('\n') + '\n' : numbered.join('\n')
}
```

**In `readPaths`:** After reading each file's content, if `lineNumbers === true`, pass the content through `prefixLineNumbers(content, 1)`.

**In `readFileRange`:** After slicing the line range (lines `startLine` to `endLine`), if `lineNumbers === true`, pass through `prefixLineNumbers(slice, startLine)` so that each prefix reflects the line's actual position in the file, not its position in the slice.

---

## Tests in `src/file/FileTools.test.ts`

All tests must follow `docs/TESTING.md`: one test per code path, atomic, offline, using temp dirs, mocking all external I/O. Each of the following is a separate `it` block:

### `prefixLineNumbers` helper (pure, no filesystem)

- **Default start offset = 1**: call `prefixLineNumbers("a\nb\nc\n")` and assert the result is `"   1 | a\n   2 | b\n   3 | c\n"`.
- **Custom start offset**: call `prefixLineNumbers("x\ny\n", 10)` and assert lines are prefixed `"  10 | x\n  11 | y\n"`.
- **No trailing newline**: call `prefixLineNumbers("a\nb")` (no trailing newline) and assert the result is `"   1 | a\n   2 | b"` (no trailing newline added).
- **Width scales for large line numbers**: call with a string of 101 lines starting at offset 1; assert line 100 is prefixed `" 100 | ..."` (4-char width) and line 101 is prefixed `" 101 | ..."`.
- **Single line**: `prefixLineNumbers("only\n")` → `"   1 | only\n"`.

### `readPaths` with `lineNumbers`

- **`lineNumbers: false` (default) — output unchanged**: create a 3-line file, call `readPaths([path])` without `lineNumbers`, assert the returned content is the raw file text (no prefix).
- **`lineNumbers: true` — lines prefixed from 1**: same file, call `readPaths([path], true)`, assert each line starts with `"   1 | "`, `"   2 | "`, `"   3 | "`.
- **Multiple files in one call**: create two files, call `readPaths([path1, path2], true)`, assert both are independently numbered starting at `1`.

### `readFileRange` with `lineNumbers`

- **`lineNumbers: false` — no prefix**: read lines 2–4 of a 10-line file without `lineNumbers`; assert content has no `|`-prefixes.
- **`lineNumbers: true` — absolute line numbers**: read lines 5–7 of a 10-line file with `lineNumbers: true`; assert the first returned line is prefixed `"   5 | ..."`, not `"   1 | ..."`.
- **Range starting at line 1**: with `lineNumbers: true`, `startLine=1` still shows `"   1 | ..."`.
- **Single-line range**: read exactly one line with `lineNumbers: true`; result is a single prefixed line.

---

## Files

- `src/file/FileTools.ts`
- `src/file/fileTypes.ts`
- `src/file/FileTools.test.ts`

features.title: P2.5 — Embed batching guidance in `grepFile` and `readFileRange` JSDoc descriptions
features.description:
## Problem

OpenCode embeds batching/cross-tool preference guidance directly inside each tool's `description` field. This means the model reads the guidance every time it sees the tool schema — not just once in the system prompt where it may be ignored or forgotten mid-task.

Our `grepFile` and `readFileRange` descriptions today say nothing about when *not* to use them. This drives the model toward serial, narrow reads instead of preferring the wider `readPaths` and the new batch tools (`readFileRanges`, `grepFiles`).

---

## Changes

### `src/file/fileTypes.ts` — update JSDoc for `grepFile` and `readFileRange`

#### `grepFile`

Append to the existing description:

```
Prefer readPaths for full file content when the file is small or when you
need multiple sections. Prefer grepFiles to run multiple patterns in a
single round-trip.
```

Full updated JSDoc example:

```ts
/**
 * Search for a regex pattern within a single file and return matching lines.
 *
 * Prefer `readPaths` for full file content when the file is small or when
 * you need multiple sections. Prefer `grepFiles` to run multiple patterns
 * (or multiple files) in a single round-trip.
 *
 * @param path Project-relative file path.
 * @param pattern Regex pattern to search for.
 */
grepFile(path: string, pattern: string): Promise<string>
```

#### `readFileRange`

Append to the existing description:

```
If you need more than 2 sections from the same file, prefer readPaths
instead. Prefer readFileRanges to read ranges from multiple files in a
single round-trip.
```

Full updated JSDoc example:

```ts
/**
 * Read a specific line range from a file.
 *
 * If you need more than 2 sections from the same file, prefer `readPaths`
 * instead (reads the whole file in one call). Prefer `readFileRanges` to
 * read ranges from multiple files in a single round-trip.
 *
 * @param path Project-relative path.
 * @param startLine 1-based start line (inclusive).
 * @param endLine 1-based end line (inclusive).
 * @param lineNumbers If true, prefix each line with its 1-based absolute
 *   line number (format: `"  42 | <content>"`). The prefix is not part of
 *   the file content and must not appear in write-tool arguments.
 */
readFileRange(path: string, startLine: number, endLine: number, lineNumbers?: boolean): Promise<string>
```

---

## Why JSDoc and not just the system prompt

The tool schema is re-transmitted on every LLM call as part of the tools array. JSDoc descriptions flow into the `ToolSchemas` auto-generated file and from there into the schema description field seen by the model at every turn — persistent reinforcement, not a one-time instruction.

---

## Tests

This feature is a JSDoc-only change to `src/file/fileTypes.ts` — no runtime behaviour changes. There are no executable tests for this feature in isolation.

**Verification is via compile check only:** after editing the JSDoc strings, run `tsc --noEmit` (or the project's `compileCheck`) to confirm the file still type-checks cleanly. Any schema-generation pipeline that reads JSDoc should also be re-run to confirm the new guidance text appears in the generated schemas.

Ensure the updated comments do **not** break any `ts-to-zod` / schema generation pipeline by running the existing `compileCheck` after making changes.

---

## Files

- `src/file/fileTypes.ts`

features.title: P2.6a — Promote `readFileRange` and `grepFile` to batch tools: `readFileRanges` and `grepFiles`
features.description:
## Problem

Agents use `readPaths` (plural, accepts an array) for reading full files. But for range reads and grep, they are forced into per-call tools: `readFileRange(path, start, end)` and `grepFile(path, pattern)`. This produces unnecessary round trips — e.g., reading 4 different ranges from 4 files costs 4 tool calls and 4 LLM turns.

The fix, consistent with how `readPaths` works, is to provide batch variants that each accept an array of queries and return all results in a single call.

---

## New Tools

### `readFileRanges`

```ts
readFileRanges(
  queries: Array<{ path: string; startLine: number; endLine: number; lineNumbers?: boolean }>,
): Promise<Array<{ path: string; startLine: number; endLine: number; content: string } | { path: string; startLine: number; endLine: number; error: string }>>
```

- Accepts an array of `{ path, startLine, endLine, lineNumbers? }` queries.
- Executes all reads concurrently (`Promise.all`).
- Returns an array in the same order as the input. Each element is either:
  - `{ path, startLine, endLine, content: string }` on success.
  - `{ path, startLine, endLine, error: string }` if the file is missing or range is invalid.
- `lineNumbers` follows the same semantics as the newly added `readFileRange` parameter: each line is prefixed with its absolute 1-based line number in the file.

**JSDoc:**
```ts
/**
 * Read multiple line ranges from one or more files in a single round-trip.
 *
 * Prefer this over multiple sequential `readFileRange` calls. Results are
 * returned in the same order as the input queries.
 *
 * If you need entire file contents, prefer `readPaths`.
 *
 * @param queries Array of range queries.
 * @param queries[].path Project-relative file path.
 * @param queries[].startLine 1-based start line (inclusive).
 * @param queries[].endLine 1-based end line (inclusive).
 * @param queries[].lineNumbers Optional. If true, prefix each line with its
 *   absolute 1-based line number (format: `"  42 | <content>"`).
 */
readFileRanges(queries: ReadFileRangesQuery[]): Promise<ReadFileRangesResult[]>
```

### `grepFiles`

```ts
grepFiles(
  queries: Array<{ path: string; pattern: string }>,
): Promise<Array<{ path: string; pattern: string; matches: string } | { path: string; pattern: string; error: string }>>
```

- Accepts an array of `{ path, pattern }` queries.
- Executes all greps concurrently (`Promise.all`).
- Returns an array in the same order as input. Each element is either:
  - `{ path, pattern, matches: string }` — same format as `grepFile` (matching lines joined as a string).
  - `{ path, pattern, error: string }` — if the file is missing or the regex is invalid.

**JSDoc:**
```ts
/**
 * Search for regex patterns across multiple files in a single round-trip.
 *
 * Prefer this over multiple sequential `grepFile` calls. Results are
 * returned in the same order as the input queries.
 *
 * Prefer `readPaths` when you need full file content rather than specific matches.
 *
 * @param queries Array of `{ path, pattern }` queries.
 * @param queries[].path Project-relative file path.
 * @param queries[].pattern Regex pattern to search for.
 */
grepFiles(queries: GrepFilesQuery[]): Promise<GrepFilesResult[]>
```

---

## Types in `src/file/fileTypes.ts`

Add these types alongside the interface additions:

```ts
export type ReadFileRangesQuery = {
  path: string
  startLine: number
  endLine: number
  lineNumbers?: boolean
}

export type ReadFileRangesResult =
  | { path: string; startLine: number; endLine: number; content: string }
  | { path: string; startLine: number; endLine: number; error: string }

export type GrepFilesQuery = {
  path: string
  pattern: string
}

export type GrepFilesResult =
  | { path: string; pattern: string; matches: string }
  | { path: string; pattern: string; error: string }
```

---

## Implementation in `src/file/FileTools.ts`

Both tools delegate to the existing single-item implementations, wrapped in `Promise.all`:

```ts
async function readFileRangesImpl(
  root: string,
  queries: ReadFileRangesQuery[],
): Promise<ReadFileRangesResult[]> {
  return Promise.all(
    queries.map(async (q) => {
      try {
        const content = await readFileRangeImpl(root, q.path, q.startLine, q.endLine, q.lineNumbers)
        return { path: q.path, startLine: q.startLine, endLine: q.endLine, content }
      } catch (e: any) {
        return { path: q.path, startLine: q.startLine, endLine: q.endLine, error: String(e?.message ?? e) }
      }
    }),
  )
}

async function grepFilesImpl(
  root: string,
  queries: GrepFilesQuery[],
): Promise<GrepFilesResult[]> {
  return Promise.all(
    queries.map(async (q) => {
      try {
        const matches = await grepFileImpl(root, q.path, q.pattern)
        return { path: q.path, pattern: q.pattern, matches }
      } catch (e: any) {
        return { path: q.path, pattern: q.pattern, error: String(e?.message ?? e) }
      }
    }),
  )
}
```

Expose in `createFileTools`:
```ts
readFileRanges: (queries) => readFileRangesImpl(ROOT, queries),
grepFiles: (queries) => grepFilesImpl(ROOT, queries),
```

---

## Single-item tools

`readFileRange` and `grepFile` **remain in the API** unchanged. The new batch variants are additive. Update their JSDoc (see P2.5 feature) to point to the batch versions.

---

## Tests in `src/file/FileTools.test.ts`

All tests must follow `docs/TESTING.md`: one test per code path, atomic, offline, using temp dirs, mocking all external I/O. Each of the following is a separate `it` block:

### `readFileRanges`

- **3-query batch returns correct content in order**: create 3 files with known content, call `readFileRanges` with one range per file; assert all 3 results contain the correct lines in the same order as the input.
- **Missing file returns `{ error }` without aborting others**: mix a valid range with a query for a non-existent file; assert the missing file entry has an `error` string and the valid entries have `content`.
- **`lineNumbers: true` in a batch query**: include one query with `lineNumbers: true`; assert that result's `content` has absolute line-number prefixes while a sibling query without `lineNumbers` does not.
- **Empty queries array returns `[]`**: call `readFileRanges([])` and assert the result is `[]`.

### `grepFiles`

- **2-query batch returns both match sets**: create 2 files each containing a distinct keyword; call `grepFiles` with one pattern per file; assert each result has a non-empty `matches` string containing the expected line.
- **No matches returns empty `matches` string (not an error)**: call `grepFiles` with a pattern that matches no lines in an existing file; assert `matches` is an empty string and there is no `error` key.
- **Invalid regex in one query returns `{ error }` for that item**: include one query with an invalid regex (e.g. `"["`) alongside a valid query; assert the bad query has `error` and the valid query has `matches`.
- **Empty queries array returns `[]`**: call `grepFiles([])` and assert the result is `[]`.

---

## Files

- `src/file/FileTools.ts`
- `src/file/fileTypes.ts`
- `src/file/FileTools.test.ts`

features.title: P2.6b — Add `searchFilesAndRead` composite tool: search + read in one round-trip
features.description:
## Problem

Today an agent that wants to find relevant files and then read their contents must make **two sequential tool calls**:
1. `searchFiles(query)` → `string[]` (list of matching paths)
2. `readPaths(paths)` → `Record<string, string>` (file contents keyed by path)

These are two LLM turns. A composite `searchFilesAndRead` collapses this into one.

The return type is fundamentally different from `searchFiles` — it returns a content map (`Record<string, string>`) not an array of paths. This is why it must be a **separate tool** rather than a parameter on `searchFiles`: agents need to know upfront whether they'll receive paths or content.

---

## New Tool: `searchFilesAndRead`

### Signature

```ts
searchFilesAndRead(
  query: string,
  path?: string,
): Promise<Record<string, string>>
```

**Parameters:**
- `query` — Same as `searchFiles`: space-separated keywords, passed directly to the underlying search.
- `path` — Optional project-relative start path to restrict the search scope (default `'.'`). Same semantics as `searchFiles`.

**Returns:** A `Record<string, string>` where each key is a project-relative file path and the value is the full file content — the same shape as `readPaths`.

---

## Implementation in `src/file/FileTools.ts`

Delegate to the existing `searchFiles` + `readPaths` internals:

```ts
async function searchFilesAndRead(
  root: string,
  projectId: string,
  query: string,
  path: string = '.',
  dbConnectionString?: string,
): Promise<Record<string, string>> {
  const paths = await searchFiles(root, projectId, query, path, dbConnectionString)
  if (paths.length === 0) return {}
  const result = await readPaths(root, paths)
  // readPaths returns FilesResult (Record<string, string | string[]>)
  // Directories would come back as string[] — coerce to a content-only map
  const contentMap: Record<string, string> = {}
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(result)) {
    if (typeof v === 'string') {
      contentMap[k] = v
    }
    // directories (string[]) are silently excluded — they have no content to show
  }
  return contentMap
}
```

Expose in `createFileTools`:
```ts
searchFilesAndRead: (query: string, path: string = '.') =>
  searchFilesAndRead(ROOT, projectId, query, path, dbConnectionString),
```

---

## Interface in `src/file/fileTypes.ts`

Add to `FileTools`:

```ts
/**
 * Search for files by name or textual content and return their full contents
 * in a single round-trip.
 *
 * Equivalent to calling `searchFiles` followed by `readPaths`, but in one
 * tool call. Use this when you need both the discovery step and the content
 * in the same turn.
 *
 * The return type is a content map (`Record<string, string>`) — **not** an
 * array of paths. Use `searchFiles` if you only need paths.
 *
 * @param query Space-separated keywords (same as `searchFiles`).
 * @param path Project-relative start path to restrict the search scope (default '.').
 * @returns Object where keys are project-relative paths and values are file contents.
 * @example
 * const files = await files.searchFilesAndRead('FileTools')
 * // { 'src/file/FileTools.ts': '...', 'src/file/fileTypes.ts': '...' }
 */
searchFilesAndRead(query: string, path?: string): Promise<Record<string, string>>
```

---

## Tests in `src/file/FileTools.test.ts`

All tests must follow `docs/TESTING.md`: one test per code path, atomic, offline, using temp dirs, mocking all external I/O. The `searchFiles` dependency must be mocked (it uses an external DB / index); test only the composition + directory-filtering logic.

Each of the following is a separate `it` block:

- **Returns content map when `searchFiles` returns matching paths**: mock `searchFiles` to return `['a.ts', 'b.ts']`, with both files present on disk; assert the returned map has both keys with string values equal to the file contents.
- **Returns `{}` when `searchFiles` returns no matches**: mock `searchFiles` to return `[]`; assert the result is `{}` and `readPaths` is never called.
- **Excludes directory entries from the result**: mock `searchFiles` to return a path that `readPaths` resolves as a `string[]` (directory listing); assert that path is **not** present in the returned map.
- **Scoped search passes `path` to `searchFiles`**: call with an explicit `path` argument; assert the underlying `searchFiles` mock was called with the same `path` value.
- **Result values are strings**: for any matched file, assert `typeof result[key] === 'string'`.

---

## Files

- `src/file/FileTools.ts`
- `src/file/fileTypes.ts`
- `src/file/FileTools.test.ts`

features.title: Explicit Batching Instructions
features.description: Update prompts and tool descriptions to explicitly instruct the coding agent to batch as many tool calls as possible per turn while still respecting execution order and dependencies. Emphasize preferring bulk operations and single-round-trip retrieval where safe.

Update src/file/FileTools.ts and all related call sites/tool schemas so these operations match the project's array-based file tool conventions.
